Help the learner talk naturally about their week.

Study Layout

Experience

🎯Lesson Goal

Help the learner talk naturally about their week, daily life, family, hobbies, work, feelings, small events, and what they want to practise next.

🌍Introduction

This is a speaking-first catch-up question sheet. The goal is not perfect English. The goal is to speak more comfortably, build longer answers, review useful daily vocabulary, and connect ideas naturally. Listening note: Normal Listen mode is not the main fit for this lesson because there is no continuous story or article audio to follow. The teacher can still model the questions aloud, and a future optional model-reading audio can be used for pronunciation practice. For the website version, this lesson should open in Study mode and show conversation questions instead of a normal listening path.

Conversation Questions

Simple Warm-Up

Start with easy questions so the learner can enter English gently.

Main question: How was your week?

Follow-up questions

  • Was it busy or relaxing?
  • Was it better than last week?
  • Why?
  • What did you do this week?
  • Did anything interesting happen?
  • How are you feeling today?

Answer help

My week was busy.

My week was relaxing.

This week I worked a lot.

Today I feel tired because I had a busy week.

Today I feel relaxed because I had time to rest.

Useful phrases

Today I feel ... because...

Tip: Use one answer-help phrase, then add your own example or reason.

Food and Daily Routine

Use food and routine because they are easy topics for longer A2 answers.

Main question: What did you eat this week that you really enjoyed?

Follow-up questions

  • Who made it?
  • Would you eat it again?
  • Did you cook anything this week?
  • Did your family like it?
  • Did your routine change this week?
  • Was the change good or difficult?

Answer help

I ate curry, and it was delicious.

My wife made it.

Yes, I cooked dinner.

It was easy because I knew the recipe.

My routine changed because I was busy.

Useful phrases

I ate ... and it was...

I cooked...

Hobbies and Free Time

Main question: Did you have time for your hobbies this week?

Answer help

No, I did not have time because I was busy.

I practised my swing.

The difficult part was staying relaxed.

To relax, I watched a movie.

Fun Questions

Use light questions when the learner has energy. Skip them if time is short.

Main question: If your week was a movie, what would the title be?

Follow-up questions

  • Why would that be the title?
  • Was it a comedy, drama, or action movie?
  • What small thing made you smile this week?
  • Who were you with?
  • What are you looking forward to next week?

Answer help

The title would be "A Busy Week."

I chose that title because I had many things to do.

I smiled when my child laughed.

Next week I am looking forward to a day off.

Maybe next week will be calmer.

Useful phrases

The title would be...

I chose that title because...

I smiled when...

Tip: Use one answer-help phrase, then add your own example or reason.

Mini Speaking Task

End with one connected answer. The learner can use the frames and add real details.

Main question: Can you talk about your week in 5 to 8 sentences?

Follow-up questions

  • Can you say what happened this week?
  • Can you name the best part?
  • Can you name one difficult thing?
  • Can you explain how you felt?
  • Can you say one thing you want to do next week?

Answer help

This week I was busy with work and family.

The best part was eating dinner with my family.

One difficult thing was waking up early.

I felt tired because I had many things to do.

Next week I want to rest more and practise English.

Useful phrases

This week I...

The best part was...

One difficult thing was...
